title: Multi-Chart Dashboard Analysis
tagline: Year 4 — Reading several metrics together (visitors, conversion, order value): orders, revenue and growth chains

introduction.overview: A dashboard shows several charts about one business: traffic, a conversion rate and an average order value. The three metrics multiply: orders = visitors × conversion, and revenue = orders × average order value. A question about revenue growth therefore needs all three charts, and a change in one metric must be separated from changes in the others. The skill is to compute the chain for each period and then compare.
introduction.placementRelevance: Dashboard-style sets are increasingly common in analytics-oriented company tests.
introduction.realWorldContext: Marketing and e-commerce teams read exactly such dashboards every week.

learningObjectives: Separate effects of traffic, conversion and value
Find the period of best performance

requiredTopics: Growth Rate and CAGR from DI
prerequisiteKnowledge.quickRefresher: Orders = visitors × conversion ÷ 100. Revenue = orders × order value. Growth = change ÷ old.

coreDefinitions: Conversion rate: share of visitors who order.
Average order value: revenue per order.
Driver: a metric that changes the result.
conceptExplanation.theoreticalIntuition: Revenue is a product of three numbers; changing any one changes the result.
conceptExplanation.visualOrMentalModel: Fill a table: orders and revenue for each month. Then compare months.

mainNarrative: January: 12,000 visitors × 2.5% = 300 orders; at ₹800 each, revenue ₹2,40,000.
February: 15,000 × 3.0% = 450 orders; at ₹820, revenue ₹3,69,000. Revenue rose 53.75% because visitors rose 25%, conversion rose 20% and order value 2.5%.
A fall in conversion can hide behind rising traffic: May has more visitors than April but a higher conversion and order value, so revenue is higher.
Always compute the chain; do not guess from one chart.

deepDiveAspects.title: Multiplicative effects
deepDiveAspects.content: Percentage changes in the three metrics multiply, not add.

deepDiveAspects.title: Rate versus count
deepDiveAspects.content: Conversion is a rate; orders are counts; do not confuse the two.

solvedExamples.title: Orders
solvedExamples.question: January: 12,000 visitors and 2.5% conversion. How many orders?

solvedExamples.title: Revenue
solvedExamples.question: 300 orders at an average of ₹800. Revenue?

solvedExamples.title: Decomposition
solvedExamples.question: Visitors rise 25% and conversion rises 20%. By what factor do orders change?

traditionalVsShortcut.shortcutMethod: Compute orders and revenue for each period once; compare drivers by their percentage changes.

placementTips.recruiterInsight: Revenue growth is usually the product of three smaller growths.
